canonical_statement: The review summarizes atopic dermatitis pathogenesis, current treatments, and emerging topical and oral JAK inhibitors.
The authors conducted a focused review using published literature, clinical trial results, case reports, abstracts, scientific-meeting presentations, and industry press releases.
The review identifies JAK-STAT signaling as a mechanistic treatment target in atopic dermatitis, particularly through cytokines including IL-4, IL-13, and IL-31.
The review states that topical and oral JAK inhibitors were being developed to address limitations of existing topical and systemic atopic dermatitis therapy.
The authors reported no funding.
Both authors reported multiple personal-fee relationships with pharmaceutical companies, and one author reported investigator funding to her institution from several companies.

In an early phase 1b trial, gusacitinib was described as safe and well tolerated, and EASI-50 and itch improvement were reported only at the highest doses.
The review states that additional trials are needed to define long-term JAK-inhibitor safety and durability.
The review states that real-world data are needed to understand outcomes in heterogeneous and racially diverse populations.
The review states that additional clinical and molecular phenotyping is needed to identify patient subgroups best suited for JAK-inhibitor therapy.
The authors conclude that JAK inhibitors are a highly promising and increasingly established therapeutic class for atopic dermatitis.
